text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi said Italy has made huge strides towards satysfying criteria for the European single currency. Prodi also said that Italy would go to next week's Amsterdam summit of EU leaders with its head high, respecting key criteria for countries wishing to join EMU (all).

* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said that Italy could enjoy better-than-expected interest rate falls if the government introduced structural spending changes. Fazio told a parliamentary commission that recent government spending targets contained in its three-year economic programme (DPEF) appeared "excessive". Fazio also said he hoped he would be able to cut interest rates but warned that the outlook appeared unsettled, saying that if he cut short-term rates there were not the conditions for a corresponding fall in market rates. He said he would only relax his current tight monetary policy as the economy gradually gained strenght (all).
* Finance minister Vincenzo Visco, speaking to a parliamentary budget commission, said that Germany's central bank policy has created unemployment in Germany and the rest of Europe (all).

* European Commissioner Karel Van Miert indicated state Italian holding IRI could be granted a further extension to a deadline on cutting its debt to levels agreed with the European Commission. The Italian Treasury said the group will hold its shereholders meeting on June 16 instead of June 13 (all).

* Alitalia managing director Domenico Cempella said that the Italian state airline recorded losses of 80 billion lire in the first four months of 1997 against 320 billion losses in the same 1996 period, adding that the group still hoped to close the 1997 year in the black (all).

* The European Commission said it had cleared the acquisition by Italian telecoms group STET of a stake in Mobilkom Austria, a mobile phone operator currently fully owned by Post und Telekom Austria AG.
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
